items.question: How soon can I be seen?
items.answer: Same-day sick visits open every weekday morning: call before 10 am. New patient visits are usually available within one to two weeks.

items.question: How do I change or cancel a visit?
items.answer: Use the link in your confirmation text or call the front desk. Please give us 24 hours so another patient can take the time.

items.question: Can I choose my clinician?
items.answer: Yes. Pick a clinician when you book, or take the first open time and we match you with whoever is available.

items.question: Do you see children?
items.answer: Yes. Our family clinicians see every age, from newborn checks to school and sports physicals.

items.question: What if it is an emergency?
items.answer: Larkspur is not an emergency service. For chest pain, trouble breathing or a serious injury, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.

items.question: Which insurance plans do you accept?
items.answer: Most major plans plus Medicare and Medicaid. Call us and we will confirm your plan before you book.

items.question: What if I do not have insurance?
items.answer: Self-pay prices are posted up front: an in-clinic visit is $120, a video visit $90 and a phone visit $60.

items.question: When will I get a bill?
items.answer: Any balance left after insurance is emailed about 30 days after your visit. Pay online, by phone or at the front desk.

items.question: Can I set up a payment plan?
items.answer: Yes. Billing can split any balance into monthly payments with no interest.

items.question: How do I request a refill?
items.answer: Ask your pharmacy to send a refill request, or call the front desk. Most refills are ready in two business days.

items.question: When will I get my lab results?
items.answer: Most results are ready in three to five business days. Your clinician calls if anything needs follow-up.

items.question: Can you send prescriptions to any pharmacy?
items.answer: Yes. Tell us your preferred pharmacy when you book and we send prescriptions there electronically.

items.question: What should I bring to my first visit?
items.answer: A photo ID, your insurance card and a list of the medicines you take. Arrive 10 minutes early to check in.

items.question: How do video visits work?
items.answer: We text you a secure link. Open it on your phone or computer a few minutes before; no app needed.

items.question: How long does a visit take?
items.answer: A routine visit is about 20 minutes with your clinician. A new patient visit takes about 40 minutes.
